  4)              In a deep learning model using deconvolution layers (also known as transposed  
  convolutions) for image generation, suppose you notice artifacts in the generated images  
  when the deconvolution kernels are initialized randomly. What effect might this have on  
  A)         the output, and how can the choice of kernel initialization (e.g., using learned filters vs. (5)  
  random initialization) and kernel size impact the model's performance? Additionally,  
  explain the potential role of padding strategies in reducing artifacts.  
  
  B)         Which deep learning technique is primarily used in neural style transfer for extracting  
  content and style features?                                                                 (3)  
  
  C)         Suppose you're using Grad-CAM to visualize the important regions for a specific class  
  prediction in a convolutional neural network. After generating the heatmap, you notice  
  that the highlighted regions appear to focus on the background rather than the object of  
  interest in the image. What might be the underlying causes for this unexpected outcome, (2)  
  and how can you modify your Grad-CAM implementation or the model itself to address  
  this issue?  
  
  5)              Discuss the role of Siamese Networks or Triplet Networks in improving verification  
  tasks. How do these architectures help CNNs learn similarity or dissimilarity between  
  (5)  
  faces for verification purposes?

  B)         In the context of action/activity recognition using deep learning, you are tasked with  
  developing a model that can recognize human activities from video footage. The video  
  frames contain various motion patterns such as walking, running, sitting, and standing.  
  Explain how 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (3D-CNNs) and Long Short-Term                  (3)  
  Memory (LSTM) networks can be utilized to address the spatio-temporal nature of  
  human activities. Discuss the advantages of combining these two approaches for more  
  accurate action recognition.
